s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance with a history of cardiac arrhythmia and pacemaker implantation
salient_findings: Gaze deviation in the right eye
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Presented to the emergency department
Has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation
Has a history of complete heart block
Has a pacemaker implanted in the late 1990s
Pacemaker was upgraded to a biventricular system
Blood pressure was 147/75 mm Hg
Heart rate was 84 beats per minute
Respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute
Oxygen saturation was 99% on room air
Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory
Electrocardiogram showed a ventricular-paced rhythm with ventricular bigeminy

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of atrial fibrillation, which is a known risk factor for cardioembolic stroke

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of atrial fibrillation and presentation with stroke symptoms make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with unilateral weakness and speech disturbance could be consistent with thrombotic stroke

shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms could be consistent with lacunar stroke, although less likely given the large middle cerebral artery territory
